title: Remove review-round narrative from test comments and names
context: Code comments and test names had accumulated review-pass framing ("found on third review pass", "found on re-review") — a changelog embedded in source code. This inline narrative becomes unreadable and stale as code evolves; the actual decision history already exists in git log and Hunch decision records. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Code comments and test names must state current behavior and non-obvious rationale only. Review discovery narrative, MR/issue references, and iteration history must not appear inline — they belong in commit messages and decision systems, not in docstrings.
consequences: Comments are shorter and focused on current behavior, not discovery timeline
Future readers get the WHY immediately without excavating review history
Prevents comment drift — changes to code don't leave stale "found on pass N" framing behind
Requires discipline: contributors must not add review-narrative framing going forward
Decision rationale is preserved in git log and Hunch, externally queryable but not buried inline
alternatives_rejected: Keep review-round framing and accept that comments accumulate narrative cruft over time
Relocate all comments to Hunch without any inline code-level explanation (loses immediate context for readers)
Use a comment format that embeds ticket numbers and MR references (creates hidden dependencies and rots when systems change)
